newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GOAL CELEBRATION PROMPTS RED CARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOAL CELEBRATION PROMPTS RED CARD.

text.p: Argentine referee Javier Castrilli, dubbed "lawman" in his own country for his hardline approach, sent a player off for celebrating a goal in a South American Supercup match on Wednesday.

Castrilli also disallowed what appeared to be a goal during a penalty shootout which decided the quarter-final between Colombia's Atletico Nacional and Santos of Brazil in the Colombian city of Medellin.
Defender Francisco Mosquera's effort for Atletico was ruled to have missed by Castrilli after bouncing down off the crossbar but replays showed that the ball had crossed the line.
Atletico striker John Jairo Trellez, booked in the first half, was shown the red card immediately after scoring in the 63rd minute because he ran across the athletics track to celebrate with fans.
Atletico went on to win the match 3-1 to level the tie at 3- 3 but were beaten 7-6 in the controversial shootout which also saw Santos goalkeeper Edinho -- Pele's son -- score for his team.
Despite the win, Santos's performance could not have been further removed from the traditions of the once great club.

The Brazilians packed their team with defenders and spent the entire match encamped in their own penalty area, refusing to venture upfield. Not even the advantage of an extra man could entice them to attack.

Edinho, who has recently been dropped only to regain his place thanks to an injury to his replacement Sergio, had a mixed night, giving away the penalty which led to Atletico's third goal after rugby-tackling an opponent.
Boca Juniors, whose $15 million team have made a mediocre start to the Argentine championship, saw their Supercup aspirations evaporate in another penalty shooout.

Coach Carlos Bilardo, whose position looks increasingly precarious, watched his team hold Brazilian championship leaders Cruzeiro to a 1-1 away draw, only to be beaten 7-6 on penalties. The first leg ended 0-0.
Argentine's Velez Sarsfield reached the semifinals by beating Paraguay's Olimpia 1-0 away, 4-0 on aggregate.
